Vanessa —

We've seen a sharp increase in both 500 errors and tail latency starting right after you pushed your latest model/quant profile this morning (around 08:45 PDT). Our p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~980ms and error rate climbed from 0.2% to ~3.8%. The error pattern is mostly decode-time OOM/timeout across hot routes.

This is impacting Checkout and Fraud-check flows; traffic is already throttled but our business needs this resolved ASAP. We collected a few traces and one example request id: req-7c9f2a. Attaching a p95 graph and the error sample.

Can you confirm whether you rolled a qprofile change or a model binary swap? We were told there would be a staged rollout.

Subject: Re: Fwd: (urgent) latency & error spike after today

Quick triage results (first-pass):
- Root cause signal: qprofile-v5 increases mixed-precision packing and changes kernel tiling that looks fine in infra tests but for Starlane’s request-size distribution it increases GPU memory jitter and causes KV cache evictions during decoding bursts. That leads to frequent fallback decoding attempts and timeouts on our hot path.
- Metrics: observed +4x variance in GPU mem high-water vs v4, correlated with p95 spike. Error class is mostly runtime-timeout (not application decode correctness).

Immediate mitigations we can apply without a full rollback (recommended order):
1) pin Starlane’s routing to qprofile-v4 (previous profile) on their production pool (zero code change, config-only). This is a fast flip.
2) temporarily reduce batch_size to 1 and disable kv_prefetch for the Starlane hotpool to reduce memory churn (can be applied cluster-side).
3) prepare a rollback script to model binary v3.9.2 if config flips don’t stabilize within 30–45 minutes.

I’m attaching a diff (qprofile-v5-diff.txt) showing the key tuning lines that increase mem packing. I can apply (1) now if we get signoff from the account owner and the customer.

—Marcus

marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Subject: Stabilization plan and proposed window for rollback

Kevin / team —

Thanks for the report and Marcus’s analysis. Proposed immediate steps:
- Step A (apply now, low-risk): pin Starlane’s fleet to qprofile-v4 and set batch_size=1 + kv_prefetch=off for the hotpool. We expect to see p95 come down within one full traffic cycle (~5–10 minutes) if memory churn is the culprit.
- Step B (if Step A fails within 30m): execute rollback-playbook.pdf to revert to model v3.9.2 across Starlane’s dedicated nodes. This is a short maintenance window; we recommend 1–2 minutes of transient throttling during the switch.

Requesting customer permission to apply Step A immediately and Step B during a low-traffic window (your call). We will monitor token-level latencies and attach a retrospective once stabilized.

I’ll open an incident page and post runbook links: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/INC-2028-358-starlane

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Aug 2028 05:45:00 +00:00
Subject: Exec summary: Starlane incident (qprofile-v5) — customer impact & next steps

Markus — quick executive summary and asks. I’m leaving the full incident timeline in the incident doc but calling out the key items here:

What happened:
- 08:40 PDT 7 Aug: qprofile-v5 rolled to Starlane fleet (config-only). 08:45 PDT: customer reported p95 jump and error-rate increase affecting Checkout/Fraud hot routes.
- Cause: qprofile-v5 memory-packing changes increased GPU memory jitter and caused KV cache evictions under Starlane’s request-size distribution, resulting in runtime timeouts.

Impact:
- Duration (customer-visible): ~40–90 minutes depending on pool; peak p95 ~980ms, error rate peaked ~3.8%. Traffic was degraded for two critical payment flows. Customer temporarily routed some flows to a cached fallback which increased friction for end users.
- Business risk: potential revenue impact in the low single-digit % at peak minutes (customer analytics are running numbers).

Actions taken:
- 09:00 PDT: pinned Starlane traffic back to qprofile-v4 and applied batch_size/buffer knobs to hotpool (Marcus/Irene). Observable p95 improvement within 7–10 minutes for most nodes.
- 09:45 PDT: rollback of variants completed where required; incident declared resolved from platform side at ~10:20 PDT.
- Post-incident: internal postmortem and perf gate added to model/quant rollout checklist for customers on heavy hotpath traffic.

Customer ask / Exec ask:
- Starlane requested a commercial credit for the impacted window and an SLA exception for the rollout cadence on their account.
- Recommend approval for a modest customer credit (I propose $12k) to preserve the relationship while we tighten rollout gating.
- Recommend we pause any further qprofile-v5 customer rollouts until we complete a targeted perf sweep and add a per-customer memory-sensitivity check.

Next steps:
1) Internal postmortem scheduled (owners: Marcus/Irene) — runbook + perf tests due EOD +3.
2) Customer-facing RCA draft and credit recommendation (owner: me) — to be shared with Starlane tomorrow.
3) Product change: add a per-customer perf validation to deployment pipeline (owner: Irene/Product).

If you’re aligned I’d like quick signoff on the credit and the release hold so we can tell Starlane the plan.

—Vanessa
